conviction_note: The Q3 numbers are new (nothing was pre-released) and the conditional 2026 guide could change, so abs_move is 6.0, above the name's ~4% results-day median because the float is thin. p_up is 44, a mild lean from inference: the guide was conditioned on no significant Middle East deterioration, gas has since nearly doubled, and O-I's Europe collapsed. The findings sum to -2.0, larger than the scaled -0.72. The gap comes from the >80% 2026 energy hedge, the October sector bounce while gas rose (the market may be pricing pass-through), and an unsourced consensus. The signs agree.

already_public.what: FY2026 guide: adjusted EBITDA ~EUR700m, FCF ~EUR220m (ex restructuring), reaffirmed with H1, conditional on no significant deterioration in the Middle East

H1 2026: revenue EUR1,699m (-1.4%), adj. EBITDA EUR352m (Q2 EUR192m, margin 21.4% vs 22.5%), inflation spread -17m in H1 after a positive Q1, Middle-East-linked cost inflation (transport, packaging) in Q2
More than 80% of 2026 energy needs hedged (Q1 release)
Q3 2025 comparison base: revenue EUR846m, adj. EBITDA EUR181m (21.3%), with weak August/September 2025 demand

new_in_release.expect: Q3 revenue and adjusted EBITDA are new. I expect EBITDA around EUR175-182m, roughly flat on the EUR181m base: restructuring savings (Essen) and an easy Aug/Sep 2025 comparison, against a negative price/cost spread and Middle East cost inflation. Slightly below the bar.

The ~EUR700m guide is reaffirmed or trimmed. It was conditional on no significant Middle East deterioration, and gas has since nearly doubled. The hedge limits the 2026 hit, so the likeliest case is 'around 700' with a stronger caveat or a low-end tilt. Skewed down.
Q4 and 2027 energy/pricing commentary will probably be held back to the 18 Nov CMD. Any statement that 2027 price increases are being pushed through would be positive, unknown.
Usually not detailed in the Q3 release; leverage ratio update likely around 2.6x. Neutral.

session_check: amc. The release is after the Paris close on 27 Oct 2026, not bmo, so the window is the 27 Oct close to the 28 Oct close. Verallia's own calendar, in the H1 release and on the IR agenda page, reads '27 octobre 2026 : résultats financiers T3 2026 - communiqué de presse après bourse et conférence téléphonique/présentation le lendemain à 9h00 CET'. Every 2026 results release was filed at 18:45 CET (Q1 22 Apr 16:45 UTC, H1 28 Jul 16:45 UTC). O-I Glass also reports on 27 Oct after the US close, which lands inside the same window. positioning_check: AMF register read (covered: true, as of 2026-10-22). No disclosed net short at or above 0.5%, and no change over ten days. This is a truncated zero, so anchor_covered is false. Building or covering is not observable: there is nothing to squeeze and no informed short flow to agree with. Ownership matters more here. BWGI holds 77.17%, Bpifrance 3.80% and the FCPE 4.04% (scrip dividend release, 2026-05-28, https://fr.ftp.opendatasoft.com/datadila/INFOFI/BWR/2026/05/FCBWR168058_20260528.pdf), so the free float is about 15%. The liquidity contract was cut from EUR5m to EUR1.2m because the float and liquidity had shrunk (https://fr.ftp.opendatasoft.com/datadila/INFOFI/BWR/2026/05/FCBWR167928_20260518.pdf). A thin float amplifies the move in either direction.

findings.finding: The 2026 guide (~EUR700m EBITDA) was explicitly conditioned on 'the absence of a significant deterioration of the situation in the Middle East'. Since then French PEG gas for November delivery rose to EUR85.88/MWh (16 Oct) from about EUR44 in mid-June, and Cal-27 went from EUR55.95 to EUR70.06 between 25 Sep and 16 Oct. That makes a trimmed or caveated guide at Q3, and a negative read on the 2027 cost base, the main risk in the release, softened by the >80% 2026 hedge.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At Q3 2025 (22 Oct 2025) Verallia cut its 2025 EBITDA guide from ~800m to ~700m and the stock moved only -0.35% the next day (23.08 to 23.00), so the cut had been largely anticipated. The 17 Feb 2026 footprint/restructuring release drew -5.7%. The H1 2026 release, guide confirmed but Q2 margin down, drew -4.7%.
findings.original_quote: Sous réserve de l'absence d'une détérioration significative de la situation au Moyen-Orient, Verallia réaffirme ses perspectives 2026, en particulier : un EBITDA ajusté d'environ 700 M€ ; un free cash-flow d'environ 220 M€ (translation: subject to no significant deterioration in the Middle East situation, Verallia reaffirms its 2026 outlook, in particular adjusted EBITDA of about EUR700m and free cash flow of about EUR220m)
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Since the 1 Oct sector low (16.35) the stock has risen to 18.27, while gas went up about 25% on the forward curve. If the market feared a guide cut, the stock would have kept falling with gas, as O-I has fallen to about $6 from $9.2 in late July. Instead it is pricing pass-through or the hedge, and the release is the first point where the company must say which. Inference from macro to company: the company has not said the condition has been triggered.

findings.finding: The company's own numbers imply H2 2026 EBITDA of about EUR348m against EUR342m in H2 2025 (+2%). Q2 2026 EBITDA was EUR192m at a 21.4% margin, down from about EUR204m (22.5%) in Q2 2025, and the inflation spread turned negative in Q2. Q3 therefore needs the trend to bend back to roughly flat against a EUR181m base. Restructuring savings (+EUR8m in Q2, Essen) and a soft Aug/Sep 2025 comparison make that possible but not given.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 EBITDA +8% (159m vs 147m) drew +6.6% the next day (19.26 to 20.54). H1 2026, flat EBITDA with the Q2 margin down, drew -4.7% (19.48 to 18.57). The quarter's EBITDA has moved this stock in both directions.
findings.original_quote: Le spread d'inflation est négatif sur le semestre (-17 M€), malgré un premier trimestre positif. [...] d'autres postes de coûts augmentent en lien avec la crise au Moyen-Orient (coûts de transport, emballage, etc.) (translation: the inflation spread was negative over the half (-EUR17m) despite a positive Q1 [...] other cost items are rising because of the Middle East crisis: transport, packaging, etc.)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The H1 reaction (-4.7%) already sold the Q2 margin slippage, and the gap lands inside what the company guided. It stays a small negative because the Middle East cost line it names has worsened since July. If the market expected a Q3 margin rebound, the stock would not sit 6% below its pre-H1 price.

findings.finding: The closest peer, O-I Glass, reported Q2 2026 European segment operating profit down 93% to $6m, citing 'competitive pricing pressure' and higher Middle-East-linked energy costs, and cut its 2026 outlook. UBS downgraded O-I to Neutral (target $11 to $6) on 5 Oct, and O-I's Q3 lands on 27 Oct after the US close, inside this window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history. The sector fell together on 1 Oct 2026 (Verallia -4.7%, Zignago about -6%, Vidrala about -4.5%), so peer read-across does move this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: O-I's Q2 is two months old and Verallia's H1 came out the same week. What is not priced is O-I's Q3 European commentary, released hours after Verallia's and read on the same session. A further European deterioration or a price war comment would stack on Verallia's own release. Industry proxy only, so sized small.

findings.finding: Pernod Ricard's Q1 FY27 (Jul-Sep 2026) showed volumes back to growth at +6% (strategic international brands +2%), though Europe came in below expectations. Spirits is the segment Verallia named as driving its volume growth in H1, accelerating in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume commentary moved the stock at Q1 2026 (+6.6% on volumes stable and EBITDA up). No case where a customer read-across alone moved it.
findings.original_quote: Volumes returned to growth at +6% (search-snippet summary of the French article; I could not open the article itself, so the exact sentence is not quoted)
findings.why_not_priced: One customer's quarter, mostly outside Europe (US -10%, China -25%, rest of world +4%). It is weakly linked to Verallia's European glass volumes and partly offset by Pernod's weaker Europe, so it is sized small. If it were a strong signal, glass peers would have re-rated on 15-16 Oct, and they moved only a little.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly negative, in line with the small negative priced lean (-0.18) but against the stock's 12% rebound off the 1 Oct low and the +3.6% 20-day run-up, which suggest the market has already looked through the gas spike. That is why p_up sits only 6 points below 50.
language_note: The guidance condition is quoted from the French regulated filing on the AMF flux; the English wire copy carries the same condition, so this was a primary source rather than unique information.

The AMF flux gave the shareholder structure after the scrip dividend (BWGI 77.17%, Bpifrance 3.80%, FCPE 4.04%) and the liquidity contract cut from EUR5m to EUR1.2m 'reflecting the change in free float'. This is what sets abs_move for a ~15% float, and the English search results did not surface it.

The French H1 release gave the Q2 cost detail (inflation spread -17m over the half, Middle-East-linked transport and packaging costs) and the 'après bourse' session wording that settled the amc window.
selectra.info (French) carried the dated PEG Nov-26 and Cal-27 settlement prices for October 2026; English search returned only September TTF levels.
lessons_applied: 'The move is in the guide' plus the first-measured European base (about 7% when the numbers are new, 9% when the guide changes): abs_move raised from 5.5 to 6.0. It stays below 7 because a reaffirmed guide is still the most likely outcome and this name's own results-day reactions run 0.35-6.6%.
'A finding that lands inside what the company already guided goes toward 0': the H2-arithmetic reported_quarter finding was cut from -0.8 to -0.4.

Applying the core's file-everything rule on re-reading the set: the Vidrala H1 fact, which the draft had left unfiled as priced, is now filed at +0.1. Not a LESSONS.md rule, but it changed the count and the sum.
Unchanged by the file: the guidance finding stays -1.5 (macro-to-company transmission keeps it small; the company's own explicit condition keeps it from being smaller), and p_up stays at 44.
